profile.mandals: Addanki, Ballikurava ,                            Janakavaram Panguluru , Korisapadu, Santhamaguluru
profile.constituencyprofile_Text:
Addanki Vision Action Plan 2024-29 has been meticulously designed to leverage the constituency's agricultural strength, dynamic industrial base, thriving construction sector, and robust service sector. This strategic blueprint aligns with Andhra Pradesh’s ambitious Swarna Andhra @ 2047 vision, which resonates with the national agenda of Viksit Bharat @ 2047.


Addanki has a rich historical and administrative legacy established as a Nagara Panchayat in 2011, the region witnessed a transformative milestone in 2022 with the upgrade to a grade 2 municipality.

Addanki Constituency has a rich historical and administrative legacy, constituting 5 Mandals, i.e., Addanki, Korisapadu, Janakavaram Panguluru, Ballikurava, and Santhamaguluru and Addanki Municipality, having a geographical area of 1075 square kilometers.

In Medieval times, the post-Kakatiya era Andhra region was ruled by many kingdoms ,among them the Reddy Rajulu kingdom was prominent.

During their reign Addanki was the capital for the Andhra Region from 1325 to 1448 AD, having a rich cultural heritage, and in Telugu poetry Yerraapragada was one among Kavithraya who translated Jyasamhitha (Maha Baratham) from Sanskrit to Telugu. The Asthana pandita belongs to the Prolaya Vema Reddy Asthana.

The inscription, a replica of the original one that was excavated near the Thousand Pillar Temple of Addanki [8], stands testimony to a flourishing Telugu literature much before the available literary texts. This is the first poem ever to be written in the Telugu language. Starting with the Boya campaign, Pandaranga got victories in all military campaigns of his master, Gunaga Vijayaditya III. The inscription spoke about the donation of land by the king to him for his successful military exploits. A noted scholar-poet of those times, he had translated Sanskrit poems into Telugu. Srinatha Mahakavi wrote Palanati Charitram during Reddy Rajas at a later period.
profile.geography: Addanki Geography is strategically located in Prakasam District within the region, benefiting from its proximity to the district, Ballikurava Granites and the Gundlakamma river & Addanki Itukabattis .The region has a mix of black cotton soil (74%) and red loamy soil (26%), supporting a variety of crops.
profile.populationDesc: Addanki has a total population of 296025 (As per Census 2011) with 85% residing in rural areas and 15% in urban areas. The constituency has 78,255 households, a scheduled caste population of 77,443 and a scheduled tribe population of 13,738 with a sex ratio of 977 females per 1,000 males. The literacy rate stands at 59.09%, indicating steady progress in education levels. The workforce is primarily engaged in agriculture, industries, handloom weaving, brick manufacturing and services.
profile.administrationDesc: Addanki is one of the six constituencies in Prakasam district. It has Ballikurava, Addanki, Korisapadu, Janakavaram Panguluru and Santhamaguluru.
profile.educationHealthcareDesc:
Addanki is an educational hub in the constituency, home to K.R.K Govt Degree and PG College, Govt Polytechnic College, Addanki Institute of Management and Science (AIMS), Community Health Center (CHC), Urban Primary Health Centers (UPHC) in urban areas, Primary Health Centers (PHC) in rural areas, and a lot of community buildings. School education is being strengthened with 100-plus schools.

 

The healthcare sector includes 7 PHCs, 37 sub-centers, 1 CHC, and 2 UPHC dispensaries, with plans to reduce maternal mortality by 50%, bring infant mortality below 10 per 1,000 live births, and achieve 100% vaccination coverage. A strong public health infrastructure ensures access to affordable and quality medical services.
profile.culturalheritageDesc: Addanki was known for its rich cultural and spiritual heritage, with key attractions such as the Singarakonda Prasanna Anjaneya Swamy Temple located at the foot of the hills of Singarakonda as dwarapalaka to the Lord Narasimha Swamy Temple, which is on the peak of the hill. It is believed that Sage Narada performed penance for Lord Narasimha Swamy, and the Lord appeared before him in the Varaha Narasimha Avatar. The Singarakonda Narasimha Swamy temple flourished during the time of the Vijayanagara kings in the 15th century. As per observation every year above 5 lakh devotees are visiting this temple.

economy_text.economy_Text: Addanki constituency Economy presents a comprehensive growth strategy to transform the constituency into an economically vibrant, investment-friendly, and employment-driven region. With a Gross Constituency Domestic Product (GCDP) of ₹7194 crores in 2023-24(FRE), Addanki is projected to achieve ₹1,56,422 crores by 2047-48, reflecting a strong and sustainable annual growth trajectory averaging 13-15%.  As of 2023-24, the economy is led by the agriculture and allied sector, contributing 51.01% to the Gross Value Added (GVA), followed by the service sector at 32.08%, and the industrial sector at 16.91%.
economy_text.gcdP_Growth_Text: Addanki  GCDP is witnessing steady economic momentum with a targeted 12-15% annual GCDP growth rate across key sectors like Agriculture, Livestock, and Horticulture. This growth trajectory aligns with the long-term vision of making the constituency a vibrant economic hub by 2047.

thrust.description: Promotion of value-added agricultural products, cold storage, and supply chain infrastructure.
Development of modern dairy farms, poultry production, and processing units.
Establishment of food processing units, packaging industries, and food parks with backward linkages to farmers.
High-yield fruit, vegetable, and floriculture production with cold chain and export linkages.
Smart townships, affordable housing, commercial hubs and facilitating urbanization, attracting private investment, and supporting infrastructure-led growth.
Solar, wind, green hydrogen, and hybrid energy projects with grid integration.
